title: Cold-tier Recovery and SIEM Export Strategy
content:
Purpose:
This working note describes the operational strategy for recovering audit records from the cold (deep archive) tier and reliably exporting them to downstream SIEMs. It focuses on practical implementation details for indexing, manifest-driven rehydration, backfill safety, and common failure modes (and mitigations). This is intended for SREs, infra engineers, and security engineers owning the audit pipeline.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to immutable audit events generated by API gateways, auth systems, and RBAC v2 changes.
- Cold tier = objects moved to archival storage (S3 Glacier / long-term blob store) after hot/warm TTLs.
- Canonical storage path and manifest metadata are available in the catalog index service.
- Downstream SIEMs expect per-event NDJSON with normalized schema and an at-least-once semantic (deduping handled on SIEM side where possible).

Background (why this doc):
We have had two recurring pain areas: 1) delayed or partial SIEM exports when on-call needs to rehydrate historical data, and 2) brittle backfills that broke ordering or created duplicates. This doc consolidates findings from two P0 incidents and a proof-of-concept rehydration job.

Key invariants and principles (must hold):
- Immutability: cold-tier objects are append-only; any replay should treat archived files as authoritative.
- Manifests drive correctness: each archive batch has a signed manifest with checksums, byte ranges, and event watermarks (min_ts, max_ts).
- Idempotency: rehydration and export jobs must be idempotent (use per-event idempotency keys + dedup windows).
- Monotonic watermarks: every archive manifest contains a watermark token that ties the manifest to the ingestion stream position; replays must honor watermark ordering when required by consumers.

Storage layout and naming conventions (canonical):
- s3://redwood-audit/{env}/{year}/{month}/{day}/shard={shard}/batch-{manifest_ts}-{uuid}.ndjson.gz
- manifests: s3://redwood-audit/{env}/{year}/{month}/{day}/shard={shard}/manifest-{manifest_ts}-{uuid}.json
  - manifest fields: batch_id, shard, item_count, checksum_sha256, min_event_ts, max_event_ts, ingestion_watermark, encryption_key_id, is_evidence_hold

Retention mapping to obligations and SLOs:
- Hot (30d): immediate queryable store, <200ms tail latency SLO for queries; used for console and quick audits.
- Warm (31-365d): still indexed for search but moved to cheaper nodes; query SLOs relaxed to <2s.
- Cold (365d+ default): archived to long-term object store; retrieval SLOs measured as rehydration completion time (target within 48 hours under normal load).
- Legal/Evidence holds override lifecycle and mark manifests with is_evidence_hold=true which prevents deletion or tiering.

Rehydration / backfill design (manifest-driven):
1) Plan: create a rehydration request referencing manifest IDs (or a date/shard range). Requests live in a control topic (kafka/queue) and create jobs in the replay service.
2) Stage 1 - manifest validation: verify manifest checksum, manifest signature, and that referenced batch file exists. If manifest missing -> fail fast with DLQ entry.
3) Stage 2 - object retrieval: request archive retrieval (expedited/standard) from object store and poll until available. Track retrieval_id and TTL.
4) Stage 3 - stream/transform: stream the ndjson.gz into the reindex worker; apply schema migrations (if replaying across schema versions) and map fields for SIEM export (normalize event_type, user_id, resource_id, action, outcome, trace_id).
5) Stage 4 - export: push into SIEM connector with per-batch transactional semantics (batch_id, sequence range). Maintain a per-shard checkpoint of last_exported_watermark.
6) Stage 5 - post-verify: verify counts and checksums against manifest; if mismatch, mark job failed and create ticket with remediation checklist.

Safety patterns and deduping:
- Each event must carry event_id and ingestion_watermark. SIEM exports include original event_id to enable deduping on the consumer side.
- Rehydration jobs publish export offsets to a durable checkpoint store; replay should not re-export ranges already checkpointed unless force=true.
- Keep an export-log (append-only) of batches pushed with checksums to enable out-of-band verification.

SIEM export specifics and constraints:
- Transform map: internal schema -> SIEM mapping layer (field normalizers, timestamp canonicalization to UTC, redaction flags).
- Batching: target 1k events or 5MB per push to SIEM endpoint, whichever comes first. Support both bulk HTTP and streaming ingestion.
- Retry policy: exponential backoff up to 24 hours, with local DLQ for permanent client-side 4xx errors.
- Ordering: for SIEMs that require ordering by time, ensure export batches respect manifest max_event_ts ordering; if cross-shard ordering is required, orchestrate a merge phase (expensive) and use only for high-value time windows.

Failure modes and runbook steps (common):
1) Missing archive object (manifest references non-existent object)
   - Symptom: manifest validation fails with 404 when fetching batch file.
   - Immediate actions: raise ticket; attempt to locate object with alternate catalog lookups; if under legal hold, escalate to storage team.
   - Long term: add automated manifest existence check during initial archive job; alert on >0.1% missing.

2) Checksum mismatch after retrieval
   - Symptom: downloaded file checksum != manifest.checksum_sha256.
   - Immediate actions: mark job failed; re-request retrieval; if repeated, mark storage corruption incident and isolate object (do not delete).
   - Mitigation: keep redundant copy policy for critical evidence manifests.

3) SIEM ingestion transient errors (502/503)
   - Symptom: batches fail with transient HTTP errors.
   - Immediate actions: backoff and retry; if queue grows, spin up dedicated export workers.
   - Mitigation: ensure idempotency keys included so retries are safe; monitor DLQ rate.

4) Ordering regressions / watermarks move backwards
   - Symptom: downstream detects event_ts earlier than previously exported watermark for a shard.
   - Immediate actions: pause export for shard; run verification against export-log.
   - Mitigation: only allow exports that advance watermark or explicitly flagged force-replay workflows with manual approval and review.

5) Partial export (counts mismatch)
   - Symptom: manifest reports N items but only M<N exported and post-verify fails.
   - Immediate actions: do not mark manifest as completed; requeue missing batches; create incident note with batch_id and slice ranges.

Operational tools & utility commands (examples):
- List manifests for day: aws s3 ls s3://redwood-audit/prod/2025/11/17/ --recursive | grep shard=3
- Trigger rehydration (cli): rw-replay start --manifests manifest-20251117-3.json --target siem-prod --priority expedited
- Check export-log: clickhouse "SELECT batch_id, shard, status, exported_at FROM audit_export_log WHERE date='2025-11-17' AND shard=3;"

Testing and validation strategy:
- Dry-run mode: transform and checksum validated but exports are written to a staging SIEM endpoint.
- Canary replays: start with a single shard + small date range, compare counts and checksums to manifest, validate in SIEM that dedup logic works.
- Chaos tests: induce object retrieval delays and SIEM transient errors in staging to measure end-to-end recovery time.

RBAC and access controls (RBAC v2 integration):
- Only roles with replay:archive_read may request rehydration. Evidence hold operations need replay:evidence_override.
- Rehydration jobs annotate exported records with operator_id (audit trail) and require MFA session tokens for manual force replays.

Metrics and alerts to add:
- manifest_validation_failure_rate > 0.05% (pager)
- average_rehydration_latency (per manifest) - SLO: 48h
- siem_export_retry_rate and dlq_rate - SLO: 99.9% success over 7d sliding window
- export_checkpoint_lag (seconds behind latest watermark) - warn at >10m, page at >1h

Open questions / next steps:
- Decide retention override policy for manifests tied to evidence holds vs. index TTLs; currently we prevent deletion but not currently copying to a special replicated bucket for higher durability.
- Design a lightweight cross-shard merge tool for rare ordered-replay needs (cost analysis required).
- Add automated manifest existence check at archive time, and a nightly reconcilier to detect drift between catalog and object-store.

Appendix: sample manifest (human readable)
- batch_id: batch-20251117-3-3c4f
- shard: 3
- item_count: 45123
- checksum_sha256: 9d2f...b7a1
- min_event_ts: 2025-11-17T00:00:00Z
- max_event_ts: 2025-11-17T23:59:59Z
- ingestion_watermark: 9876543210
- is_evidence_hold: false

If this approach looks good I will open a short-lived RFC with storage/observability/infrastructure to capture interface contracts (manifest schema, checkpoint store API) and a small POC to run a full-day rehydrate->SIEM export against staging.

Notes to reviewers:
- Please call out missing edge cases where manifest signing or replay auth might cause operational friction.
